title: 𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃
part: Copy A, the lower gate · columns I–IV
draftNote: The letters follow one published reading of the stone and are still to be checked against photographs; two readings (I 1, I 16) depart from it, as the notes there say.
about: Around 700 BCE Azatiwada, a governor under the king of Adana in Cilicia, built a fortress on a hill above the Ceyhan river and carved his account of his deeds on its gates in two languages: the local Luwian, in Anatolian hieroglyphs, and Phoenician, the language of trade and diplomacy along the coast. This is the Phoenician. It is the longest Phoenician inscription ever found, and close kin to biblical Hebrew — a Hebrew reader will recognize most of its words. The same text in Luwian is in the library too: each section here links to its twin.
source: KARATEPE, Phoenician version, copy A (the lower gate), columns I–IV, complete (KAI 26 A; Gibson, Textbook of Syrian Semitic Inscriptions III no. 15). Found in 1946–47, so no edition before 1930 exists; following the policy adopted for the Luwian, the sequence of letters on the stone is treated as a fact, taken from the reading published by DEAPS (Digital Editions of Aramaic and Phoenician Sources, Ohio State University; 'Phoe. Class 2026' edition, following Gibson 1988), and still to be checked against photographs. Two departures, in I 1 and I 16, are explained in their notes; letters the source restores in damaged places (III 1–2) are printed, and the note says so. The two other copies (C, on the statue of the god; B, fragments) are not printed; where C differs in substance, a note says so. Line numbers give the column and the stone line where each section begins; words the stone breaks over a line end are printed whole. The stone leaves no spaces between words; the spaces here follow the editions. Vocalization (the line under the letters) is reconstructed — Phoenician wrote no vowels — after the conventions of the standard grammars, and applied consistently; the actual vowels are unknown in many words. The Hebrew-letters switch shows the same consonants in the square script. Translations are made fresh from the Phoenician; no modern translation was consulted. Font: Noto Sans Phoenician (OFL).

sentences.t: 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃 𐤄𐤁𐤓𐤊 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤏𐤁𐤃 𐤁𐤏𐤋
sentences.tr: ʾanōkī ʾAzitiwadda habbarūk Baʿl, ʿebed Baʿl
sentences.l: I (am) Azatiwada, the-blessed of-Baal, servant of-Baal,
sentences.i: I am Azatiwada, blessed of Baal, servant of Baal,
sentences.n: No verb 'am': Phoenician, like Hebrew, sets a name beside 'I' and lets the sentence stand. אנכ is Hebrew אנכי, written without its final vowel letter — Phoenician spells only consonants, even at the end of a word. Baal here is the god the Luwian calls Tarhunzas, the storm god. The source we follow prints ʿbr in the last word; we read ʿbd, 'servant', which the Luwian ('servant of Tarhunzas') requires — on this stone r and d are almost the same letter.

sentences.t: 𐤀𐤔 𐤀𐤃𐤓 𐤀𐤅𐤓𐤊 𐤌𐤋𐤊 𐤃𐤍𐤍𐤉𐤌
sentences.tr: ʾiš ʾiddir ʾAwarik milk Dānunīm
sentences.l: whom made-mighty Awariku, king of-the-Danunians.
sentences.i: whom Awariku, king of the Danunians, raised to power.
sentences.n: אש is the relative 'who, whom, which' — Hebrew אשר without its last letter. The verb comes before its subject, the usual order. מלכ 'king' was pronounced milk, judging from how Greek and Latin writers spelled Phoenician names. The Danunians are the people of Adana, the kingdom the Luwian calls Hiyawa.

sentences.t: 𐤐𐤏𐤋𐤍 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤋𐤃𐤍𐤍𐤉𐤌 𐤋𐤀𐤁 𐤅𐤋𐤀𐤌
sentences.tr: paʿalanī Baʿl la-Dānunīm la-ʾab wa-la-ʾimm
sentences.l: Made-me Baal for-the-Danunians into-a-father and-into-a-mother.
sentences.i: Baal made me a father and a mother to the Danunians.
sentences.n: פעל 'do, make' is Phoenician's everyday verb where Hebrew uses עשה; the נ on the end is 'me'. ל… ל: 'make someone into something'. The Luwian says 'mother and father', in the other order.

sentences.t: 𐤉𐤇𐤅 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤀𐤉𐤕 𐤃𐤍𐤍𐤉𐤌
sentences.tr: yaḥwō ʾanōkī ʾiyyat Dānunīm
sentences.l: Gave-life I the-Danunians.
sentences.i: I gave the Danunians life.
sentences.n: You'll see this constantly: a bare verb form (the infinitive) followed by אנכ 'I' is this text's way of saying 'I did it' — the whole boast is told in this pattern. אית marks the object, like Hebrew את.

sentences.t: 𐤉𐤓𐤇𐤁 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤀𐤓𐤑 𐤏𐤌𐤒 𐤀𐤃𐤍 𐤋𐤌𐤌𐤑𐤀 𐤔𐤌𐤔 𐤅𐤏𐤃 𐤌𐤁𐤀𐤉
sentences.tr: yarḥeb ʾanōkī ʾarṣ ʿimq ʾAdana la-mimṣaʾ šamš wa-ʿad mabōʾiyu
sentences.l: Widened I the-land of-the-Plain of-Adana from-the-going-out of-the-sun and-as-far-as its-coming-in.
sentences.i: I widened the land of the plain of Adana from sunrise to sunset.
sentences.n: The sun 'goes out' in the east and 'comes in' in the west, as in Hebrew ממזרח שמש עד מבואו. The י on מבאי means 'its' here, not 'my' — see line 11. The Plain of Adana is the Cilician plain around the modern city of Adana.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤊𐤍 𐤁𐤉𐤌𐤕𐤉 𐤊𐤋 𐤍𐤏𐤌 𐤋𐤃𐤍𐤍𐤉𐤌 𐤅𐤔𐤁𐤏 𐤅𐤌𐤍𐤏𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-kūn ba-yamūtiya kull nuʿm la-Dānunīm wa-šabʿ wa-manʿam
sentences.l: And-there-was in-my-days every good for-the-Danunians, and-plenty and-delight.
sentences.i: In my days the Danunians had every good thing, plenty and comfort.
sentences.n: כנ, from the root kwn, is Phoenician's 'be', where Hebrew uses היה. ימת 'days' has the plural ending -ōt, as in poetic Hebrew ימות.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤌𐤋𐤀 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤏𐤒𐤓𐤕 𐤐𐤏𐤓
sentences.tr: wa-millōʾ ʾanōkī ʿaqarōt Paʿar
sentences.l: And-filled I the-storehouses of-Paʿar.
sentences.i: I filled the granaries of Paʿar.
sentences.n: עקרת is a rare word; the Luwian has 'granaries' at this point, which fixes the sense. פער is a place, the Luwian Pahar.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤐𐤏𐤋 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤎𐤎 𐤏𐤋 𐤎𐤎 𐤅𐤌𐤂𐤍 𐤏𐤋 𐤌𐤂𐤍 𐤅𐤌𐤇𐤍𐤕 𐤏𐤋 𐤌𐤇𐤍𐤕 𐤁𐤏𐤁𐤓 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤅𐤀𐤋𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-paʿōl ʾanōkī sūs ʿal sūs wa-magen ʿal magen wa-maḥanet ʿal maḥanet ba-ʿabūr Baʿl wa-ʾilīm
sentences.l: And-made I horse upon horse and-shield upon shield and-camp upon camp, for-the-sake-of Baal and-the-gods.
sentences.i: I piled up horse on horse, shield on shield, army on army, by the grace of Baal and the gods.
sentences.n: The Phoenician runs horse, shield, army; the Luwian horse, army, shield. מחנת is Hebrew מחנה, a camp and the army in it. בעבר is Hebrew בעבור 'for the sake of'. 'By the grace of Baal and the gods' has no counterpart in the Luwian here; in the Phoenician it returns as a refrain.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤔𐤁𐤓𐤕 𐤌𐤋𐤑𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-šibbartī malīṣīm
sentences.l: And-I-broke the-scoffers,
sentences.i: I broke the insolent,
sentences.n: A change of form: שברת is an ordinary past tense with the ending ת 'I', in place of the infinitive-plus-אנכ pattern. מלצמ is uncertain — 'scoffers' or 'the insolent', from the root of Hebrew לץ. The Luwian clause is just as uncertain, so the two versions cannot settle each other here.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤕𐤓𐤒 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤊𐤋 𐤄𐤓𐤏 𐤀𐤔 𐤊𐤍 𐤁𐤀𐤓𐤑
sentences.tr: wa-tarōq ʾanōkī kull ha-raʿ ʾiš kūn ba-ʾarṣ
sentences.l: and-cleared-out I all the-evil that was in-the-land.
sentences.i: and I cleared away all the evil that was in the land.
sentences.n: The root of תרק is uncertain; the sense 'cleared out' is safe because the Luwian says 'drove out of the land'.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤉𐤈𐤍𐤀 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤁𐤕 𐤀𐤃𐤍𐤉 𐤁𐤍𐤏𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-yaṭnōʾ ʾanōkī bēt ʾadōnī ba-nuʿm
sentences.l: And-set-up I the-house of-my-lord in-goodness,
sentences.i: I established my lord’s house in prosperity,
sentences.n: יטנא is the causative (Phoenician makes it with י where Hebrew uses ה) of a root meaning 'raise'. בת is 'house', Hebrew בית: Phoenician writes the contracted vowel without its י. 'My lord' is Awariku.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤐𐤏𐤋 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤋𐤔𐤓𐤔 𐤀𐤃𐤍𐤉 𐤍𐤏𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-paʿōl ʾanōkī la-šurš ʾadōnī nuʿm
sentences.l: and-did I for-the-root of-my-lord good,
sentences.i: and I did good to my lord’s line,
sentences.n: שרש 'root' means descendants, as in Hebrew שרש ישי.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤉𐤔𐤁 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤏𐤋 𐤊𐤎𐤀 𐤀𐤁𐤉
sentences.tr: wa-yašōb ʾanōkī ʿal kissiʾ ʾabīyu
sentences.l: and-seated I (him) on the-throne of-his-father.
sentences.i: and I set him on his father’s throne.
sentences.n: A false friend for Hebrew readers: אבי here is 'his father', not 'my father'. After a noun ending in the genitive vowel -i, Phoenician writes 'his' as י (-yu). ישב is the causative, 'make sit' (Hebrew הושיב).

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤔𐤕 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤔𐤋𐤌 𐤀𐤕 𐤊𐤋 𐤌𐤋𐤊
sentences.tr: wa-šōt ʾanōkī šalōm ʾitt kull milk
sentences.l: And-made I peace with every king.
sentences.i: I made peace with every king,
sentences.n: שת 'put, make' is Hebrew שית; את is here the preposition 'with'. This clause is lost from both copies of the Luwian (§17); only the Phoenician keeps it.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤀𐤐 𐤁𐤀𐤁𐤕 𐤐𐤏𐤋𐤍 𐤊𐤋 𐤌𐤋𐤊 𐤁𐤑𐤃𐤒𐤉 𐤁𐤇𐤊𐤌𐤕𐤉 𐤅𐤁𐤍𐤏𐤌 𐤋𐤁𐤉
sentences.tr: wa-ʾap ba-ʾabūt paʿalūnī kull milk ba-ṣidqī ba-ḥokmatī wa-ba-nuʿm libbī
sentences.l: And-also in-fatherhood made-me every king, because-of-my-righteousness, because-of-my-wisdom, and-because-of-the-goodness of-my-heart.
sentences.i: and every king even treated me as a father, for my justice, my wisdom and the goodness of my heart.
sentences.n: Here the final י is 'my' (ṣidqī, ḥokmatī, libbī), against 'his' in אבי (line 11): the letter is the same, and the vowel before it decides. The Luwian of this clause is broken; its gaps are restored from this Phoenician sentence.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤁𐤍 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤇𐤌𐤉𐤕 𐤏𐤆𐤕 𐤁𐤊𐤋 𐤒𐤑𐤉𐤕 𐤏𐤋 𐤂𐤁𐤋𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-banō ʾanōkī ḥōmiyōt ʿazzōt ba-kull qaṣayōt ʿal gabūlīm
sentences.l: And-built I walls strong at-all the-ends, on the-borders,
sentences.i: I built strong walls at all the far ends, on the frontiers,
sentences.n: חמית 'walls' is Hebrew חומות; קצית 'ends, edges' is Hebrew קצות; גבלמ 'borders' is Hebrew גבולים.

sentences.t: 𐤁𐤌𐤒𐤌𐤌 𐤁𐤀𐤔 𐤊𐤍 𐤀𐤔𐤌 𐤓𐤏𐤌 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤀𐤂𐤃𐤃𐤌
sentences.tr: ba-maqōmīm ba-ʾiš kūn ʾišīm raʿīm baʿlē ʾagdūdīm
sentences.l: in-places in-which were men bad, masters of-bands,
sentences.i: in places where there had been bad men, leaders of gangs,
sentences.n: באש is ב 'in' plus the relative אש: 'in which'. אשמ is 'men' (Hebrew אנשים). בעל here is the ordinary noun, 'master, owner' — the same word as the god's name. אגדדמ: 'bands, troops', the root of Hebrew גדוד.

sentences.t: 𐤀𐤔 𐤁𐤋 𐤀𐤔 𐤏𐤁𐤃 𐤊𐤍 𐤋𐤁𐤕 𐤌𐤐𐤔
sentences.tr: ʾiš bal ʾiš ʿabd kūn la-bēt Mopš
sentences.l: who — not a-man (of them) a-servant was to-the-house of-Mopsos.
sentences.i: not one of whom had ever been subject to the house of Mopsos.
sentences.n: בל 'not' is the negative of Hebrew poetry (בל ימוט). מפש is Mopsos, the seer whom Greek legend makes the founder of cities in Cilicia; the Luwian calls him Muksas. This is one of the few places where a figure of Greek myth turns up in a contemporary inscription.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃 𐤔𐤕𐤍𐤌 𐤕𐤇𐤕 𐤐𐤏𐤌𐤉
sentences.tr: wa-ʾanōkī ʾAzitiwadda šatōnōm taḥt paʿmēya
sentences.l: And-I, Azatiwada, put-them under my-feet.
sentences.i: I, Azatiwada, put them under my feet.
sentences.n: The bad men of the last line are the 'them'. שתנמ is the verb שת 'put' (see line 11) with -nōm, 'them'. פעמ is Hebrew פעם in its old sense 'foot, step' (Judges 5:28 פעמי מרכבותיו). The source we follow prints the name here as ʾztwn, which must be a slip: it is ʾztwd everywhere else, and we print it so.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤁𐤍 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤇𐤌𐤉𐤕 𐤁𐤌𐤒𐤌𐤌 𐤄𐤌𐤕 𐤋𐤔𐤁𐤕𐤍𐤌 𐤃𐤍𐤍𐤉𐤌 𐤁𐤍𐤇𐤕 𐤋𐤁𐤍𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-banō ʾanōkī ḥōmiyōt ba-maqōmīm hummat la-šibtinōm Dānunīm ba-naḥat libbinōm
sentences.l: And-built I walls in-places those, for-their-dwelling, the-Danunians, in-ease of-their-heart.
sentences.i: I built fortresses in those places so that the Danunians could live there with their minds at ease.
sentences.n: המת 'those' is Hebrew המה used as a pointer. לשבתנמ: ל + the infinitive 'to dwell' + -nōm 'their', so 'for their dwelling'. נחת לב, 'ease of heart', returns several times as the inscription's phrase for peace of mind; Hebrew has נחת in the same sense (Eccl 4:6 מלא כף נחת).

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤏𐤍 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤀𐤓𐤑𐤕 𐤏𐤆𐤕 𐤁𐤌𐤁𐤀 𐤔𐤌𐤔 𐤀𐤔 𐤁𐤋 𐤏𐤍 𐤊𐤋 𐤄𐤌𐤋𐤊𐤌 𐤀𐤔 𐤊𐤍 𐤋𐤐𐤍𐤉
sentences.tr: wa-ʿannō ʾanōkī ʾaraṣōt ʿazzōt ba-mabōʾ šamš ʾiš bal ʿinnū kull ham-milakīm ʾiš kūn lapanaya
sentences.l: And-subdued I lands strong in-the-coming-in of-the-sun, which not subdued any of-the-kings who were before-me.
sentences.i: I subdued strong lands in the west, which none of the kings before me had subdued.
sentences.n: ענ is the D-stem of the root of Hebrew ענה 'be low': 'make low, subdue'. 'The coming-in of the sun' is the west, as in line 4. ארצת: Phoenician plural of ארץ, with -ōt where Hebrew has ארצות.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃 𐤏𐤍𐤕𐤍𐤌 𐤉𐤓𐤃𐤌 𐤀𐤍𐤊
sentences.tr: wa-ʾanōkī ʾAzitiwadda ʿinnītinōm yōridōm ʾanōkī
sentences.l: And-I, Azatiwada, I-subdued-them; brought-down-them I.
sentences.i: I, Azatiwada, subdued them; I brought them down,
sentences.n: Two ways of saying 'I did' side by side: ענתנמ is a normal past tense (-ti 'I' + -nōm 'them'), ירדמ אנכ the infinitive-plus-אנכ pattern of the opening lines. ירד here is causative, 'make go down' (Hebrew הוריד): he resettled them from their highland strongholds.

sentences.t: 𐤉𐤔𐤁𐤌 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤁𐤒𐤑𐤕 𐤂𐤁𐤋𐤉 𐤁𐤌𐤑𐤀 𐤔𐤌𐤔 𐤅𐤃𐤍𐤍𐤉𐤌 𐤉𐤔𐤁𐤕 𐤔𐤌
sentences.tr: yašōbōm ʾanōkī ba-qaṣṣōt gabūlaya ba-mōṣaʾ šamš wa-Dānunīm yašabtī šam
sentences.l: Settled-them I at-the-ends of-my-borders in-the-going-out of-the-sun, and-Danunians I-settled there.
sentences.i: and settled them at the far end of my borders in the east, and I settled Danunians there.
sentences.n: An exchange of populations: conquered westerners moved east, Danunians moved in where they had been. ישב is causative, 'make dwell' (Hebrew הושיב), here with -m 'them'. שמ is 'there' (Hebrew שם), a different word from שמ 'name', which follows soon.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤊𐤍 𐤁𐤉𐤌𐤕𐤉 𐤁𐤊𐤋 𐤂𐤁𐤋 𐤏𐤌𐤒 𐤀𐤃𐤍 𐤋𐤌𐤌𐤑𐤀 𐤔𐤌𐤔 𐤅𐤏𐤃 𐤌𐤁𐤀𐤉
sentences.tr: wa-kūnū ba-yamūtiya ba-kull gabūl ʿimq ʾAdana la-mimṣaʾ šamš wa-ʿad mabōʾiyu
sentences.l: And-they-were in-my-days in-all the-territory of-the-Plain of-Adana, from-the-going-out of-the-sun and-up-to its-coming-in.
sentences.i: In my days they were throughout the territory of the Plain of Adana, from sunrise to sunset.
sentences.n: The sunrise-to-sunset phrase of line 4 again: the Danunians now live from one end of the plain to the other. גבל, Hebrew גבול, is both 'border' and the land the border encloses.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤁𐤌𐤒𐤌𐤌 𐤀𐤔 𐤊𐤍 𐤋𐤐𐤍𐤌 𐤍𐤔𐤕𐤏𐤌 𐤀𐤔 𐤉𐤔𐤕𐤏 𐤀𐤃𐤌 𐤋𐤋𐤊𐤕 𐤃𐤓𐤊
sentences.tr: wa-ba-maqōmīm ʾiš kūn lapanīm naštaʿīm ʾiš yištaʿ ʾadam la-lekt darkk
sentences.l: And-in-places that were formerly feared, where would-fear a-man to-walk a-road,
sentences.i: And in places that used to be feared, where a man was afraid to travel the road,
sentences.n: נשתעמ and ישתע come from a root šʿy/štʿ 'fear', the root of Hebrew תשתע in Isaiah 41:10 (אל תשתע). לפנמ 'formerly' is לפני 'before' without the suffix. אדמ is 'a man, a person', Hebrew אדם. The sentence breaks off and is completed by the next line.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤁𐤉𐤌𐤕𐤉 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤀𐤎𐤕 𐤕𐤊 𐤋𐤇𐤃𐤉 𐤃𐤋 𐤐𐤋𐤊𐤌 𐤁𐤏𐤁𐤓 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤅𐤀𐤋𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-ba-yamūtiya ʾanōkī ʾišt tikk laḥuddiya dal pilakkīm ba-ʿabūr Baʿl wa-ʾilīm
sentences.l: in-my-days, mine, a-woman walks by-herself, holder of-spindles, by-the-grace of-Baal and-the-gods.
sentences.i: in my own days a woman goes about on her own, spindles in hand, by the grace of Baal and the gods.
sentences.n: The best-known line of the inscription: the roads are so safe that a woman can travel alone. ימתי אנכ, 'my days, I', puts weight on 'my' — my days, unlike the kings' before me. אסת 'woman' is Hebrew אשה, Phoenician אשת; our source prints it with ס, and editions differ over the letter here. תכ 'she walks' is the verb of Hebrew הלך, with the l swallowed. לחדי 'by herself' is from חד 'one', like Hebrew לבדה. דל פלכמ, 'holder of spindles': פלך is the spindle of Proverbs 31:19, וכפיה תמכו פלך. Spinning was done on the move, so a woman with her spindle is a woman about her ordinary business.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤊𐤍 𐤁𐤊𐤋 𐤉𐤌𐤕𐤉 𐤔𐤁𐤏 𐤅𐤌𐤍𐤏𐤌 𐤅𐤔𐤁𐤕 𐤍𐤏𐤌𐤕 𐤅𐤍𐤇𐤕 𐤋𐤁 𐤋𐤃𐤍𐤉𐤌 𐤅𐤋𐤊𐤋 𐤏𐤌𐤒 𐤀𐤃𐤍
sentences.tr: wa-kūn ba-kull yamūtiya šabʿ wa-manʿam wa-šebet naʿimōt wa-naḥat libb la-Dānunīm wa-la-kull ʿimq ʾAdana
sentences.l: And-there-was in-all my-days plenty and-delight and-dwelling pleasant and-ease of-heart for-the-Danunians and-for-all the-Plain of-Adana.
sentences.i: All my days the Danunians and the whole Plain of Adana had plenty and comfort, good living and peace of mind.
sentences.n: שבת נעמת, 'pleasant dwelling', is the noun of ישב 'dwell'. The stone spells the people here דנימ, with one נ, against דננימ everywhere else: a stonecutter's shortcut or slip, kept as carved.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤁𐤍 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤄𐤒𐤓𐤕 𐤆 𐤅𐤔𐤕 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤔𐤌 𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃𐤉
sentences.tr: wa-banō ʾanōkī haq-qart zē wa-šōt ʾanōkī šumō ʾAzitiwaddiya
sentences.l: And-built I the-city this, and-put I its-name Azatiwadaya,
sentences.i: I built this city and gave it the name Azatiwadaya,
sentences.n: קרת 'city' is the word in Carthage (Qart-ḥadašt, 'New City') and Hebrew קריה/קרת (Prov 9:3 מרמי קרת). ז 'this' follows its noun, like Hebrew הזה. שמ is 'its name': Phoenician writes the suffix -ō without a letter. The city is the fortress on the hill, today's Karatepe.

sentences.t: 𐤊 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤅𐤓𐤔𐤐 𐤑𐤐𐤓𐤌 𐤔𐤋𐤇𐤍 𐤋𐤁𐤍𐤕
sentences.tr: kī Baʿl wa-Rašp Ṣipparīm šalaḥūnī la-banōt
sentences.l: for Baal and-Reshef of-the-Birds sent-me to-build.
sentences.i: for Baal and Reshef-of-the-Birds sent me to build it.
sentences.n: כ 'for, because' is Hebrew כי. Reshef is the plague and war god known from the Bible (Hab 3:5 ויצא רשף לרגליו); 'of the birds' (or perhaps 'of the goats') is a local title, and the Luwian puts its own stag god, Runtiyas, in his place. שלחנ: 'they sent' + -nī 'me'.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤁𐤍𐤉 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤁𐤏𐤁𐤓 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤅𐤁𐤏𐤁𐤓 𐤓𐤔𐤐 𐤑𐤐𐤓𐤌 𐤁𐤔𐤁𐤏 𐤅𐤁𐤌𐤍𐤏𐤌 𐤅𐤁𐤔𐤁𐤕 𐤍𐤏𐤌𐤕 𐤅𐤁𐤍𐤇𐤕 𐤋𐤁 𐤋𐤊𐤍𐤉 𐤌𐤔𐤌𐤓 𐤋𐤏𐤌𐤒 𐤀𐤃𐤍 𐤅𐤋𐤁𐤕 𐤌𐤐𐤔
sentences.tr: wa-banōyu ʾanōkī ba-ʿabūr Baʿl wa-ba-ʿabūr Rašp Ṣipparīm ba-šabʿ wa-ba-manʿam wa-ba-šebet naʿimōt wa-ba-naḥat libb la-kōnī mišmar la-ʿimq ʾAdana wa-la-bēt Mopš
sentences.l: And-built-it I, by-the-grace of-Baal and-by-the-grace of-Reshef of-the-Birds, in-plenty and-in-delight and-in-dwelling pleasant and-in-ease of-heart, for-its-being a-guard for-the-Plain of-Adana and-for-the-house of-Mopsos.
sentences.i: I built it, by the grace of Baal and of Reshef-of-the-Birds, in plenty and comfort, good living and peace of mind, to be a guard for the Plain of Adana and the house of Mopsos.
sentences.n: ובני: the י on the verb is 'it' (-yu, as in אבי 'his father'). לכני is 'for its being': ל + the infinitive of כנ + 'its'. משמר 'guard, watch' is Hebrew משמר.

sentences.t: 𐤊 𐤁𐤉𐤌𐤕𐤉 𐤊𐤍 𐤋𐤀𐤓𐤑 𐤏𐤌𐤒 𐤀𐤃𐤍 𐤔𐤁𐤏 𐤅𐤌𐤍𐤏𐤌 𐤅𐤁𐤋 𐤊𐤍 𐤌𐤕𐤌 𐤋𐤃𐤍𐤍𐤉𐤌 𐤋𐤋 𐤁𐤉𐤌𐤕𐤉
sentences.tr: kī ba-yamūtiya kūn la-ʾarṣ ʿimq ʾAdana šabʿ wa-manʿam wa-bal kūn mattam la-Dānunīm lēl ba-yamūtiya
sentences.l: For in-my-days there-was to-the-land of-the-Plain of-Adana plenty and-delight, and-not was ever to-the-Danunians night in-my-days.
sentences.i: For in my days the land of the Plain of Adana had plenty and comfort, and the Danunians never knew a night in my days.
sentences.n: The last clause is one of the inscription's puzzles. לל is 'night' (Hebrew ליל); מתמ is most often taken as 'ever, at all'. 'Night' would then be a night of fear or want, which in Azatiwada's days never came. Other readings have been proposed; the sense is uncertain.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤁𐤍 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤄𐤒𐤓𐤕 𐤆 𐤔𐤕 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤔𐤌 𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃𐤉 𐤉𐤔𐤁 𐤀𐤍𐤊 𐤁𐤍 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤊𐤓𐤍𐤕𐤓𐤉𐤔
sentences.tr: wa-banō ʾanōkī haq-qart zē šōt ʾanōkī šumō ʾAzitiwaddiya yašōb ʾanōkī bā Baʿl KRNTRYŠ
sentences.l: And-built I the-city this; put I its-name Azatiwadaya; settled I in-it Baal KRNTRYŠ.
sentences.i: I built this city and named it Azatiwadaya, and I installed in it Baal KRNTRYŠ.
sentences.n: The building report repeats, and now the god moves in. KRNTRYŠ is a local title of Baal that no one has explained; its vowels are unknown, so we print the consonants. בנ is 'in it' (ב + -n-, the suffix Phoenician uses after a preposition). The statue's copy (C) says instead 'I set up this god, Baal KRNTRYŠ' — the statue itself.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤉𐤋𐤊 𐤆𐤁𐤇 𐤋𐤊𐤋 𐤄𐤌𐤎𐤊𐤕 𐤆𐤁𐤇 𐤉𐤌𐤌 𐤀𐤋𐤐 𐤅𐤁𐤏𐤕 𐤇𐤓𐤔 𐤔 𐤅𐤁𐤏𐤕 𐤒𐤑𐤓 𐤔
sentences.tr: wa-yilik zabḥ la-kull ham-massēkōt zabḥ yamīm ʾalp wa-ba-ʿitt ḥarš śē wa-ba-ʿitt qaṣīr śē
sentences.l: And-shall-go a-sacrifice to-all the-cast-images(?): the-sacrifice of-days an-ox, and-at-the-time of-ploughing a-sheep, and-at-the-time of-harvest a-sheep.
sentences.i: And a sacrifice shall be brought to all the cast images(?): for the yearly sacrifice an ox, at ploughing time a sheep, and at harvest time a sheep.
sentences.n: ילכ 'shall go' is the verb of Hebrew הלך, as with תכ above. המסכת is uncertain: 'the cast images' (Hebrew מסכה) or 'the libations' (from נסך). זבח יממ, 'sacrifice of days', is the annual sacrifice, as in 1 Samuel 1:21 זבח הימים. ש is Hebrew שה 'a sheep or goat'. The words for 'time' and 'ploughing' are damaged in this copy and restored from copy C.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤁𐤓𐤊 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤊𐤓𐤍𐤕𐤓𐤉𐤔 𐤀𐤉𐤕 𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃 𐤇𐤉𐤌 𐤅𐤔𐤋𐤌 𐤅𐤏𐤆 𐤀𐤃𐤓 𐤏𐤋 𐤊𐤋 𐤌𐤋𐤊
sentences.tr: wa-barik Baʿl KRNTRYŠ ʾiyyat ʾAzitiwadda ḥayyīm wa-šalōm wa-ʿōz ʾaddir ʿal kull milk
sentences.l: And-may-bless Baal KRNTRYŠ Azatiwada (with) life and-peace and-power mighty over every king.
sentences.i: May Baal KRNTRYŠ bless Azatiwada with life, peace, and mighty power over every king,
sentences.n: Blessings follow the building report, as in the Luwian. ברכ with two objects: bless someone (with) something. עז אדר 'mighty power': the same אדר as 'made mighty' in line 2, here an adjective, Hebrew אדיר.

sentences.t: 𐤋𐤕𐤕𐤉 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤊𐤓𐤍𐤕𐤓𐤉𐤔 𐤅𐤊𐤋 𐤀𐤋𐤍 𐤒𐤓𐤕 𐤋𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃 𐤀𐤓𐤊 𐤉𐤌𐤌 𐤅𐤓𐤁 𐤔𐤍𐤕 𐤅𐤓𐤔𐤀𐤕 𐤍𐤏𐤌𐤕 𐤅𐤏𐤆 𐤀𐤃𐤓 𐤏𐤋 𐤊𐤋 𐤌𐤋𐤊
sentences.tr: la-tittiya Baʿl KRNTRYŠ wa-kull ʾilōnē qart la-ʾAzitiwadda ʾurk yamīm wa-rob šanōt wa-rušaʾt naʿimōt wa-ʿōz ʾaddir ʿal kull milk
sentences.l: that-may-give Baal KRNTRYŠ and-all the-gods of-the-city to-Azatiwada length of-days and-abundance of-years and-sovereignty(?) pleasant and-power mighty over every king.
sentences.i: and may Baal KRNTRYŠ and all the gods of the city give Azatiwada long life, many years, a happy reign(?), and mighty power over every king.
sentences.n: ארכ יממ 'length of days' is the Hebrew phrase (Ps 23:6 לארך ימים). אלנ is a plural of 'god' (אלמ is the other); קרת 'city' again. רשאת is uncertain; it is usually tied to ראש 'head' — headship, or the best of something.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤊𐤍 𐤄𐤒𐤓𐤕 𐤆 𐤁𐤏𐤋𐤕 𐤔𐤁𐤏 𐤅𐤕𐤓𐤔
sentences.tr: wa-kūn haq-qart zē baʿlat šabʿ wa-tirōš
sentences.l: And-may-be the-city this owner of-plenty and-new-wine,
sentences.i: May this city have plenty and wine,
sentences.n: בעל and its feminine בעלת, 'owner', make 'having' phrases: a city that owns plenty and wine. תרש is Hebrew תירוש, new wine.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤏𐤌 𐤆 𐤀𐤔 𐤉𐤔𐤁 𐤁𐤍 𐤉𐤊𐤍 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤀𐤋𐤐𐤌 𐤅𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤑𐤀𐤍 𐤅𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤔𐤁𐤏 𐤅𐤕𐤓𐤔
sentences.tr: wa-ʿam zē ʾiš yōšeb bā yakūn baʿl ʾalpīm wa-baʿl ṣōn wa-baʿl šabʿ wa-tirōš
sentences.l: and-the-people this who dwell in-it may-be owners of-oxen and-owners of-flocks and-owners of-plenty and-new-wine;
sentences.i: and may the people who live in it own oxen and flocks, plenty and wine;
sentences.n: אלפ 'ox' is the Hebrew אלף of Psalm 8:8 (צנה ואלפים), and the name of the letter 𐤀, which began as an ox's head. ישב here is the plain verb 'dwell', against the causative 'settle' of line II 18.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤁𐤓𐤁𐤌 𐤉𐤋𐤃 𐤅𐤁𐤓𐤁𐤌 𐤉𐤀𐤃𐤓 𐤅𐤁𐤓𐤁𐤌 𐤉𐤏𐤁𐤃 𐤋𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃 𐤅𐤋𐤁𐤕 𐤌𐤐𐤔 𐤁𐤏𐤁𐤓 𐤁𐤏𐤋 𐤅𐤀𐤋𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-ba-rabbīm yalidū wa-ba-rabbīm yaʾdirū wa-ba-rabbīm yaʿbudū la-ʾAzitiwadda wa-la-bēt Mopš ba-ʿabūr Baʿl wa-ʾilīm
sentences.l: and-in-multitudes may-they-bear, and-in-multitudes may-they-be-mighty, and-in-multitudes may-they-serve Azatiwada and-the-house of-Mopsos, by-the-grace of-Baal and-the-gods.
sentences.i: may they have children in great numbers, grow mighty in great numbers, and serve Azatiwada and the house of Mopsos in great numbers, by the grace of Baal and the gods.
sentences.n: ברבמ 'in multitudes' is ב + רבים. עבד ל, 'serve', takes ל, as in Hebrew. The house of Mopsos returns from line 16 of column I, now as the dynasty Azatiwada serves.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤀𐤌 𐤌𐤋𐤊 𐤁𐤌𐤋𐤊𐤌 𐤅𐤓𐤆𐤍 𐤁𐤓𐤆𐤍𐤌 𐤀𐤌 𐤀𐤃𐤌 𐤀𐤔 𐤀𐤃𐤌 𐤔𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-ʾim milk ba-milakīm wa-rōzin ba-rōzanīm ʾim ʾadam ʾiš ʾadam šum
sentences.l: And-if a-king among-kings or-a-prince among-princes, if a-man who (is) a-man of-name,
sentences.i: Now if any king among kings, or prince among princes, or any man who is a man of renown
sentences.n: The curse begins. רזנ 'prince, ruler' is the Hebrew רוזן (Judges 5:3 האזינו רזנים). 'A man of name' is a man of standing, as in Genesis 6:4 אנשי השם.

sentences.t: 𐤀𐤔 𐤉𐤌𐤇 𐤔𐤌 𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃 𐤁𐤔𐤏𐤓 𐤆 𐤅𐤔𐤕 𐤔𐤌
sentences.tr: ʾiš yimḥ šum ʾAzitiwadda ba-šaʿr zē wa-šōt šumō
sentences.l: who erases the-name of-Azatiwada on-the-gate this and-puts his-name,
sentences.i: erases Azatiwada’s name from this gate and puts his own name there,
sentences.n: מחה 'wipe out' is the verb of Exodus 17:14, מחה אמחה את זכר עמלק. The inscription is carved on the gateway's orthostats, so 'this gate' is the very stone the reader faces. שמ: 'his name', with -ō unwritten.

sentences.t: 𐤀𐤌 𐤀𐤐 𐤉𐤇𐤌𐤃 𐤀𐤉𐤕 𐤄𐤒𐤓𐤕 𐤆 𐤅𐤉𐤎𐤏 𐤄𐤔𐤏𐤓 𐤆 𐤀𐤔 𐤐𐤏𐤋 𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃
sentences.tr: ʾim ʾap yaḥmud ʾiyyat haq-qart zē wa-yissaʿ haš-šaʿr zē ʾiš paʿal ʾAzitiwadda
sentences.l: if even he-covets the-city this and-pulls-out the-gate this which made Azatiwada
sentences.i: or if he covets this city and tears out this gate that Azatiwada made
sentences.n: חמד 'covet' is the verb of the Tenth Commandment, לא תחמד. נסע, Hebrew 'set out', has its older sense here: pull up, uproot, as tent pegs are pulled up.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤉𐤐𐤏𐤋 𐤋𐤔𐤏𐤓 𐤆𐤓 𐤅𐤔𐤕 𐤔𐤌 𐤏𐤋𐤉
sentences.tr: wa-yipʿal la-šaʿr zār wa-šōt šumō ʿalēyu
sentences.l: and-makes (it) into-a-gate foreign and-puts his-name on-it —
sentences.i: and turns it into a strange gate and puts his name on it —
sentences.n: זר 'foreign, other' is Hebrew זר: a gate that belongs to someone else. עלי 'on it' (-yu again).

sentences.t: 𐤀𐤌 𐤁𐤇𐤌𐤃𐤕 𐤉𐤎𐤏 𐤀𐤌 𐤁𐤔𐤍𐤕 𐤅𐤁𐤓𐤏 𐤉𐤎𐤏 𐤄𐤔𐤏𐤓 𐤆
sentences.tr: ʾim ba-ḥimdat yissaʿ ʾim ba-śinʾat wa-ba-raʿ yissaʿ haš-šaʿr zē
sentences.l: whether out-of-desire he-pulls-out, whether out-of-hatred and-out-of-evil he-pulls-out the-gate this —
sentences.i: whether he tears out this gate out of greed, or out of hatred and malice —
sentences.n: אמ… אמ, 'whether… or', as in Hebrew אם… אם. שנת is Hebrew שנאה 'hatred', the א not written.

sentences.t: 𐤅𐤌𐤇 𐤁𐤏𐤋𐤔𐤌𐤌 𐤅𐤀𐤋 𐤒𐤍 𐤀𐤓𐤑 𐤅𐤔𐤌𐤔 𐤏𐤋𐤌 𐤅𐤊𐤋 𐤃𐤓 𐤁𐤍 𐤀𐤋𐤌 𐤀𐤉𐤕 𐤄𐤌𐤌𐤋𐤊𐤕 𐤄𐤀 𐤅𐤀𐤉𐤕 𐤄𐤌𐤋𐤊 𐤄𐤀 𐤅𐤀𐤉𐤕 𐤀𐤃𐤌 𐤄𐤀 𐤀𐤔 𐤀𐤃𐤌 𐤔𐤌
sentences.tr: wa-maḥā Baʿlšamēm wa-ʾEl qōnē ʾarṣ wa-Šamš ʿōlam wa-kull dōr banē ʾilīm ʾiyyat ham-mamlakt hāʾ wa-ʾiyyat ham-milk hāʾ wa-ʾiyyat ʾadam hāʾ ʾiš ʾadam šum
sentences.l: then-may-erase Baal-of-the-Heavens and-El, creator of-earth, and-the-Sun of-eternity, and-all the-circle of-the-sons of-the-gods, that kingdom and that king and that man who (is) a-man of-name.
sentences.i: then may Baal of the Heavens, El creator of the earth, the Eternal Sun and the whole circle of the gods wipe out that kingdom, that king and that man of renown.
sentences.n: Four witnesses to the curse, and a Hebrew reader knows two of them: אל קנ ארצ is the title of Genesis 14:19, אל עליון קנה שמים וארץ, and דר בנ אלמ, 'the circle of the sons of the gods', is the divine council of Psalm 82 and Job 1:6. הא 'that' (Hebrew ההוא) follows its noun, like ז 'this'. The verb ומח is singular though its subjects are many: the verb agrees with the first, Baal of the Heavens.

sentences.t: 𐤀𐤐𐤎 𐤔𐤌 𐤀𐤆𐤕𐤅𐤃 𐤉𐤊𐤍 𐤋𐤏𐤋𐤌 𐤊𐤌 𐤔𐤌 𐤔𐤌𐤔 𐤅𐤉𐤓𐤇
sentences.tr: ʾepes šum ʾAzitiwadda yakūn la-ʿōlam kam šum šamš wa-yariḥ
sentences.l: Only the-name of-Azatiwada shall-be forever, like the-name of-the-sun and-the-moon.
sentences.i: But Azatiwada’s name shall last forever, like the name of the sun and the moon.
sentences.n: אפס 'only, but' is Hebrew אפס (Num 22:35 ואפס את הדבר). The closing wish echoes Psalm 72:17, of the king: יהי שמו לעולם לפני שמש ינין שמו.

glossary.𐤁𐤔𐤍𐤕: ba- + śinʾat — out of hatred (Hebrew שנאה; the א unwritten)
